questions.question: When is it legal to drive on the shoulder of the road?

options.text: To overtake a vehicle
Only during daylight hours when a vehicle is driving slowly and it's safe to do so
Never, it's always illegal

questions.explanation: This is allowed to ease traffic flow, but only if it's safe.

questions.question: What does a red triangle with a cow symbol indicate?

options.text: A veterinary clinic ahead
A farm area with a possibility of animals on the road
A meat processing plant

questions.explanation: The red triangle indicates a warning for potential animal hazards.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a vehicle’s rearview mirrors?

options.text: To monitor the road behind you
To check for personal grooming
To observe passengers in the back seat

questions.explanation: Rearview mirrors are designed to enhance situational awareness.

questions.question: When approaching a railway crossing with no boom gate, what must you do?

options.text: Speed up to cross quickly
Stop, look both ways, and only proceed if it's safe
Honk your horn to alert the train driver

questions.explanation: This ensures the tracks are clear and safe to cross.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop and proceed only when it is safe
Treat it as a green light
Stop and wait for assistance

questions.explanation: This functions like a stop sign, ensuring safe movement.

questions.question: What does the term "blind spot" mean?

options.text: The area not visible in your rearview or side mirrors
The section of the road with poor lighting
A shaded area where drivers are advised to stop

questions.explanation: This is why shoulder checks are important when changing lanes.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle's brakes fail while driving?

options.text: Shift to a lower gear and use the handbrake gently
Accelerate to stabilize the vehicle
Turn off the engine immediately

questions.explanation: This helps reduce speed safely without causing a skid.

questions.question: What does a solid white line in the centre of the road mean?

options.text: Overtaking is allowed when the road is clear
Overtaking is not allowed under any circumstances
Pedestrian crossing ahead

questions.explanation: Solid lines indicate no overtaking to maintain safety.

questions.question: What is the speed limit in a residential area unless otherwise indicated?

options.text: 50 km/h
60 km/h
40 km/h

questions.explanation: The video gives 50 km/h. Corrected: the NaTIS manual sets a general speed limit of 60 km/h on every public road in an urban area unless a road traffic sign shows otherwise. There is no separate 50 km/h default for residential areas.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Rules of the Road §6.27 Speed limits (p.24)

questions.question: When driving in heavy rain, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your high beams for better visibility
Reduce your speed and increase the following distance
Use hazard lights while driving

questions.explanation: This ensures better control and reaction time in slippery conditions.
